reviews.title: App Crash
reviews.text:
Overall, I love the app, so you may be wondering why the two-star rating.

For the first time in several months of use, the app crashed after I received a phone call during a recording. I lost everything it had recorded up to that point, and I didn’t realize the app had stopped recording, so I also lost everything discussed after the call. This is a major failure in my opinion.

This was extremely frustrating as I’d relied heavily on the app to generate meeting notes, and because of the crash, I walked away from an important meeting without the information I needed for my own use.

The overall concept and intent of the app is fantastic, and when it works, it’s incredibly useful. However, losing an entire recording because of something as normal as receiving a phone call is a serious flaw that needs to be addressed.

reviews.title: Keeps crashing during recordings
reviews.text:
I paid for this app because I use it to record and summarise my university lectures, but unfortunately it keeps crashing in the middle of recordings. This is extremely frustrating because lectures can’t simply be repeated, and I need to be able to trust that the app will continue recording without suddenly closing.

When it works, I really like the app and find the transcription and summary features useful, which is why I paid for it in the first place. However, an audio recording/note-taking app needs to be reliable during long recordings. At the moment, I’m constantly worried that it will crash and I’ll lose part of an important lecture.

I really hope the developers can fix the stability issues because the app has a lot of potential, but right now I can’t rely on it for something as important as my university lectures.

reviews.title: Very Poor Quality Transcripts
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like this app because it has a lot of potential, but after using it for several months, I’m extremely disappointed.

The biggest issue is speaker identification (diarization). I regularly record business meetings with 6–8 participants, yet the transcripts typically identify only 2–3 speakers. Multiple people are merged into the same speaker label, making it nearly impossible to determine who actually said what. In some cases, male and female speakers are also incorrectly identified. This significantly reduces the value of the transcripts for professional use.

What has been even more frustrating is the lack of customer support. I have reported this issue multiple times over several months and have sent detailed examples explaining the problem. I even followed up asking whether the issue had been reproduced, whether improvements were planned, or if there were recommended recording settings that could help. Unfortunately, I have received little to no meaningful response.

I understand that no software is perfect, but acknowledging customer feedback and providing updates goes a long way. Instead, I was left wondering whether my reports were ever reviewed.

If your meetings involve only one or two people, this app may work well. However, if you depend on accurate speaker attribution in meetings with multiple participants, be aware that the current speaker identification can be unreliable.

Until the company significantly improves speaker diarization and becomes

I hope the company improves both its support availability and communication regarding user data and account activity.
